Portfolio overview

Rent outlook

Projected rent for each calendar year, applying each lease’s annual escalator on its adjustment date. Two views: current lease terms only, and with every renewal option exercised.

Projected annual rent

Bars show rent collected in each calendar year. The dashed line is today’s annual run-rate.

Lease expiration schedule

What Scioto owns

The portfolio by property type, lease structure and year of purchase.

Properties by property type

Share of properties. Click a slice to see them on the map.

Annual rent by lease type

NNN is triple net; Mod is modified gross; Full is full service.

Cap rate by lease type

Current annual rent and rent at purchase, each divided by total capitalized cost (building, land and renovations).

Lease TypeLeasesAnnual RentTotal Capitalized CostCap Rate TodayCap Rate At PurchaseChange

NNN rent is close to net operating income because tenants pay taxes, insurance and repairs. For Mod and Full leases Scioto pays some of those costs, so their true cap rates are lower than shown. Vacant homes have no current rent.

Acquisition basis by year of purchase

Capital deployed in properties still owned today, by the year they were bought.

    Re-leasing

    Vacant homes to re-lease, and leases coming up for renewal.

    Vacant homes

    Homes with no current lease. Last rent is from the prior quarter’s schedule where available; otherwise it’s estimated from the initial rent and escalator. Click a home to open it on the map.

    Expiring leases

    Leases ending soon, with their renewal options and notice deadlines. Leases with no options left are the ones most likely to need re-leasing.

    Renewal options are shown as written in the schedule (for example “2, 5 year auto”); the schedule doesn’t record options already used. “Holdovers” are leases past their expiration date that are still paying rent.
